A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Gaussian-avatar research, renamed from GAST to SeqAvatar. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original DNA-Rendering and I3D-Human experiments, component and sampling ablations, and supplementary novel-pose rendering results.

after.justification: v2 reports original rendering experiments and ablations, including additional ZJU-MoCap results, cross-sequence pose examples and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The core motion-conditioning, KNN sampling, temporal sampling and skinning pipeline remains. However, Section 9 enlarges point-motion embeddings from 64 to 96 dimensions and replaces the two-layer non-rigid MLP with three hidden layers plus an output layer. Sections 4.3 and 10 also introduce position and covariance isometry regularizers. These refine the existing method; STMS largely reorganizes already-present sampling components.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on six ZJU-MoCap sequences representing controlled motion and tight clothing, extending the previous loose-garment coverage. It also adds cross-sequence pose transfer with unseen motion patterns. Ordinary I3D-Human novel-pose rendering already appeared in v1's appendix and is not new coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding DNA-Rendering comparisons retain 3DGS-Avatar, GART and GauHuman; I3D-Human novel-view and novel-pose comparisons retain Dyco, 3DGS-Avatar and GauHuman. The added benchmark and analyses reuse these comparators. Revised scores and additional citations do not establish new baseline methods.

E3.justification: Section 8 changes DNA-Rendering's stated resolution from 512×612 for experiments to 512×612 for training and 750×1024 for testing. v2 also introduces ZJU-MoCap and cross-sequence pose-transfer protocols and changes the KNN sensitivity sweep from {1,3,6,8} to {1,5,8,10}. These are substantive reported evaluation changes, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds an out-of-distribution pose-transfer test in Figure 6 and a computational-cost analysis in Section 14. The KNN sensitivity study now tests beyond eight neighbors and reports SSIM and LPIPS alongside PSNR. The component and temporal-stride ablations already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both present point estimates or averages without statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark, baseline and ablation values are revised. For example, the matched novel-pose tables, v1 Table 4 and v2 Table 3, change the proposed method's PSNR from 30.39 to 30.28 and LPIPS×1000 from 38.15 to 36.07. v2 also adds ZJU-MoCap, cross-sequence and computational results. Method and protocol revisions prevent interpreting all numerical changes as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds mathematical definitions of position and covariance isometry penalties in supplementary Equations 35–36. The existing skinning, Gaussian-rendering and relative-rotation derivations remain substantively unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The hierarchical-motion avatar contribution remains central. v2 removes v1's explicit claim to the first sequential Gaussian-avatar framework and adds an abstract-level claim of orders-of-magnitude faster rendering than temporal NeRF approaches with comparable or superior quality. This changes the claimed quality–efficiency contribution without redefining the central research problem.

C2.justification: Section 6 replaces the needle-like-artifact discussion with blur versus NeRF's volumetric integration and adds a specific limitation: SMPL-derived velocity cues may miss fine garment deformation compared with dense surface tracking. v2 also interprets its new controlled-scene and cross-sequence experiments as evidence of generalization.

D1.justification: v2 adds DNA-Rendering frame-selection details, including training poses 0–99 and 20 evaluation time steps, plus ReLU activations and five-neighbor isometry specifications. It also supplies ZJU-MoCap sequence identifiers, a 4090 GPU specification, preprocessing timing and a project-page link. These extend the existing implementation documentation; the temporal selection details are newly disclosed rather than demonstrated changes.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning through neural-rendering work on anti-aliasing, sparse views, pose-free optimization and acceleration, and distinguishes 3D avatars from diffusion-based image animation. Added references include Mip-NeRF, BARF, MagicAnimate and isometry-related work; ASH and several former future-work references disappear. This exceeds bibliographic updating.

P1.justification: v2 renames the method and title, extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction and related work, and reorganizes spatial KNN and temporal sampling under STMS in Section 4.2. Novel-pose evaluation moves into the main text, and the supplementary narrative is reorganized around the expanded evaluation.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is updated and moved before the abstract. The I3D-Human novel-view figure moves to the supplement, while novel-pose comparisons are redesigned for the main text. New cross-sequence and ZJU-MoCap figures, benchmark and efficiency tables, and an expanded KNN table substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 better supports generalization and practical-efficiency claims through cross-sequence pose tests, ZJU-MoCap comparisons and measured computational costs, while identifying a concrete SMPL-motion limitation. These provide useful but bounded gains over v1's existing evaluation. The benefit is tempered by the total-loss equation omitting the newly described regularizers, while changed evaluation settings prevent treating all revised scores as clean performance improvements.
